note: Notation (x,y) used instead of dot product x·y for inner products; identical verbatim quote. English e01 additionally bundles the (O,y)=0 remark (c=0 in homogeneity); z35 omits it, but the identified object (the inner-product notation) is the same.
Complex Euclidean space = unitary space, example V_n(C). Both quotes match verbatim.
Complex inner product: same axioms as real except symmetry replaced by (x,y)=conj(y,x); homogeneity scalar can be complex, companion relation (x,cy)=conj(c)(x,y). Same object.

GRANULARITY DIVERGENCE (EN finer): English split the definition of a real inner product into two objects — e34 (the definition statement, axiomatic not by formula) and e09 (the four axioms listed and 'regarded as axioms'). Chinese merged both into a single z42, whose two quotes come one from e34 and one from e09. Same underlying object; the four axioms (symmetry, distributivity, homogeneity, positivity) coincide.
Real linear space with an inner product = real Euclidean space. Verbatim quote match.

Weighted integral inner product on C(a,b) with weight function w (EXAMPLE 4). No Chinese counterpart was extracted; z03 only covers the unweighted EXAMPLE 3. Extraction-coverage gap, not a language artifact.

KEY STRESS POINT (inner product vs dot product): the concrete dot product x·y in V_n (Ch.12), model that the general inner product generalizes, (x,y)=x·y in V_n. Chinese z01 KEPT the dot product (点积) as a distinct object rather than merging it into the inner-product objects — distinction preserved, no same-name-different-thing.
Orthogonal set: (x,y)=0 for every pair of distinct elements. Identical defining quote. e21 adds the trigonometric-system example; core definition identical.
THEOREM 15.9: norm properties (a)-(d), independent of choice of inner product. Same theorem.
THEOREM 15.12 Parseval's formula: (x,y)=Σ(x,e_i)conj(y,e_i) for an orthonormal basis, x=y giving ||x||^2=Σ|(x,e_i)|^2. Same theorem.

GRANULARITY DIVERGENCE (ZH finer): z34 extracts Parseval Eq (15.11) (x,y)=Σ(x,e_i)conj(y,e_i) as a standalone NOTATION object; English folded this into the theorem e25. Same mathematical content, different type classification (notation vs theorem).

GRANULARITY DIVERGENCE (ZH finer): z47 is Eq (15.12) ||x||^2=Σ|(x,e_i)|^2, the x=y specialization of Parseval, extracted as a standalone NOTATION object. English e25 states it only as the 'taking x=y' case. Special case of the general Parseval formula e25 (also a type-flip: notation vs theorem).
THEOREM 15.8 Cauchy-Schwarz: |(x,y)|^2<=(x,x)(y,y), equality iff dependent, norm form |(x,y)|<=||x|| ||y||. Same theorem.
THEOREM 15.11: components relative to an orthogonal basis c_j=(x,e_j)/(e_j,e_j); orthonormal case c_j=(x,e_j). Same theorem.

GRANULARITY DIVERGENCE (ZH finer): z45 extracts Eq (15.8) c_j=(x,e_j)/(e_j,e_j) as a standalone NOTATION object; English folded this into theorem e31. Same content, different type (notation vs theorem).

NORM/LENGTH check: norm ||x||=(x,x)^{1/2}, the metric notion of length, depends on choice of inner product. Both languages keep a single 'norm/范数' object (length as the metric concept, not a separate object). No split. Same object.
Angle between two nonzero elements, cosθ=(x,y)/(||x|| ||y||) via Cauchy-Schwarz. No Chinese counterpart extracted. Extraction-coverage gap.
Triangle inequality (Theorem 15.9 part (d)) ||x+y||<=||x||+||y|| with equality when x=O, y=O, or y=cx for c>0. Same object; verbatim equality-condition quote.
Euclidean space unqualified = real or complex; theorems hold in either case. Same object. e47 adds the 'inner product introduces the metric concept of length' remark; core convention identical.
Double-bar notation ||x|| for the norm, used to state Cauchy-Schwarz |(x,y)|<=||x|| ||y||. Same notation object.

ORTHOGONAL/PERPENDICULAR check: two elements orthogonal iff inner product zero; zero element orthogonal to all and only self-orthogonal element. Both use 'orthogonal/正交' — no spurious split into perpendicular/垂直. Verbatim quotes. Same object.
THEOREM 15.10: every orthogonal set of nonzero elements is independent; n such elements form a basis when dim V=n. Same theorem.
Unweighted integral inner product (f,g)=∫f(t)g(t)dt on C(a,b) (EXAMPLE 3); f(t),g(t) as components, integration replacing summation. Same object.
Orthonormal set = orthogonal set with each element of norm 1; normalize by dividing by norm. Verbatim quotes. Same object.

Definition of an ORTHONORMAL BASIS (正交规范基) as an orthogonal basis whose elements have norm 1. English list has no dedicated orthonormal-basis object (it appears only as a hypothesis inside e25/e31). Extraction-coverage / granularity gap on the ZH side.

Definition/existence of an ORTHOGONAL BASIS (正交基): a basis that is also an orthogonal set; every finite-dimensional Euclidean space has one. English has no matching object — e60 (Thm 15.10) is the independence theorem, not the orthogonal-basis definition, and e31 only uses it as a hypothesis. Extraction-coverage / granularity gap on the ZH side.
